sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early
sources.text: New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early. "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first." For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result. Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it. If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too . If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.title: Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game
sources.text: GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive. "Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media . It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy. "Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted. Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure. For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot . But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag. Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page . Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

sources.title: Should you spare Arnold in GTA 6?
sources.text: Your choice to spare or kill Arnold in GTA 6 has consequences In the mission 'Hey Arnold!' you face the story's first major moral dilemma: do you kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6? After Brian's shady business associate, Arnold, goes dark during GTA 6 Chapter 1 , Jason, Brian, and Cal hunt him down to the radar station near the Aerostat. It turns out Arnold isn't very happy with Brian's drug-dealing tactics and, after some heated words, Arnold and his goons jump into a pickup truck and speed off. But no one disrespects Brian like that, not on Jason's watch, and a high speed car chase immediately ensues. When the chase ends, you must choose whether to let Arnold live or execute him, with your choice impacting your GTA 6 criminal profile . If you continue chasing Arnold to the Key Lento Marina, he abandons his vehicle and Brian tells Jason to "shut him up." Though, he doesn't specify how. He simply says: "Do whatever you have to do." You then need to chase after Arnold on foot (hopefully you've been working on your fitness) until you get close enough to tackle him or he reaches the end of the pier and has nowhere else to run. He then begins to beg Jason for his life. To spare Arnold, hold down L2/LT to interact with him and press X/A to select the option to 'Spare' him. Instead of killing Arnold, Jason will threaten him and let him go. In return, you receive a contribution toward the Restrained criminal profile and Arnold scuttles off, with Brian none the wiser. There are two ways you can kill Arnold in this GTA 6 mission . The first is to complete the car chase to the Marina and then follow Arnold on foot until he reaches the end of the pier or you're able tackle him to the ground. However, when he starts begging for his life, you can instead execute him with your weapon. If you do this, you receive a warning that "Indiscriminate violence will contribute toward a violent criminal profile." If you'd rather not deal with Arnold's begging – or a pesky foot chase – you can kill Arnold by shooting at his vehicle and/or him during the car chase. Killing Arnold in this way is quicker, but contributes toward a Ruthless criminal profile. Whichever choice you make, the following cutscene will be the same. sources.title: GTA 6 Shows Why You Should Never, Ever, Ever Text and Drive (Ever)
sources.text: If you need to check Snapmatic, pull over You can pull off a lot of heinous crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Stealing a car, mugging an old lady at gunpoint, killing a bird and then beating up a cop with its corpse. All of those are sure to earn you at least a one-star Wanted level. But there’s an even worse crime in GTA 6 that you’ll probably wind up doing more than murder: texting and driving. The most important tools that Jason and Lucia have in GTA 6 are their cell phones. Rockstar makes much of the game’s UI elements diegetic by cleverly cramming them into phone apps. People will text you mission locations to explain why quest markers are appearing on the map. A news app full of absurd stories will teach you Leonida lore without you needing to find scattered logs. You’ll even manage your workout routine through a fitness app. You can easily get distracted by your phone in-game, just as you would in real life. Rockstar Games deliberately plays into that with one of GTA 6 ’s most devious features. You can pull out your phone at any time and use it in first-person – and that includes while driving. Pick up your phone behind the wheel, and you’ll barely be able to see out your windshield as your focus is drawn to your glowing screen. It's one of the many small, but effective ways that GTA 6 lampoons everyday life in the 2020s. Considering that driving already requires care and attention, the task becomes even more difficult with a phone in one hand. You’ll find yourself swerving more erratically, and most assuredly getting into accidents. I have read-ended cars and run down pedestrians because I was too busy liking memes on Snapmatic. I’m not proud of that; scratched my damn car! What’s especially devilish about the system is that GTA 6 constantly tempts you to pick up your phone. Jason and Lucia will get text messages ad nauseam. Sometimes they’ll learn an important story detail, or get the location of a mission location they’ve been waiting for. Other times, Jason might just get a friendly text from Lucia asking what he’s up to. As an obsessive communicator, I always felt like I needed to respond right away or else I’d wind up leaving these people hanging. So anytime I’d get a text while driving, I’d look at the road, determine when I could look down for just a second, and then fire off a reply. And every time, I would wind up skidding over a bridge. You can argue, as many politicians and panicked parents have for decades, that GTA glorifies a lot of bad behavior. This, on the other hand, is probably the closest that the series has ever come to approaching a dangerous real-world act like a PSA. You absolutely should not text and drive in GTA 6 , just as you should not in real life. It doesn’t matter how quickly you can speed read a text; things happen quickly on the road. I mean, one time a drunk dude on a tractor cut me off out of nowhere! If you need to check Snapmatic, pull over to the side of the road and listen to some talk radio while you text. You wouldn’t want to mess up that paint job of the car you’re about to fence after stealing it from an old lady by beating her unconscious, right? Stay cool, follow the rules!

sources.title: Where Is GTA 6's Disney World Parody? Rockstar North Co-Studio Head Explains No-Show
sources.text: GTA 6 lacks a parody of Disney World partially because developer Rockstar felt there wasn't a strong enough narrative justification for all the work that would have to go into meeting player expectations. In an interview with VGC , Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson was asked why GTA 6 doesn't feature a Disney World parody . He noted that the team didn't think it supported the game's narrative and tone enough to make it worth the time and effort. “The obvious reason?” Nelson said with a laugh, “It’s about whether there’s a narrative reason to spend that time to make a fully functioning theme park. We just figure out what we do need to support the story and support the feeling of being in Leonida. A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there." This sense that Rockstar had a blank check for GTA 6's development is something Nelson has pushed back on multiple times in the run up to the game's launch. Nelson recently touched on this issue in an interview with IGN , where he conceded that Rockstar's development approach did have to be managed, because without any guardrails, “every team will go crazy and go on forever.” “And so there’s a bit of a contract there between all of us, including ourselves; having checks and balances in terms of where we push, how far we push, how hard we push, and how much resource [something] is worth, because everything is time and resource spent,” he said. “And contrary to what people think, we don’t have infinite money or time, or resource. So we do have to make decisions.” VGC asked whether the decision to steer clear of Disney World was rooted in having to decide how many rides there would be, how fun they actually are, and making it all worthwhile. "Yeah, that’s the challenge: where do you stop?" said Nelson. "When do you feel like it’s enough? We went as hard as we could on interiors, but you’ve got to fill them – they have to feel natural.” GTA 5 allowed players to visit a pier which had a ferris wheel and a rollercoaster, and these rides were pretty boring. It was something to do one time and then never think about ever again. If you're going to a parody of Disney World, it would need to feel massive and alive so that it lives up to the hype. Rockstar has been pretty forthcoming about its decisions to not include certain things, in spite of the game being massive and freeing. GTA 6 doesn't allow you to pick up prostitutes , for example. This is a staple of the franchise and this decision has rubbed some people the wrong way. Rockstar, however, believes it is counter-intuitive to the story it is trying to tell about two protagonists who are madly in love. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? stories.title: Now That I've Played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, Here's What I Want Out of the PC Version
stories.summary: After playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, I'm forming a clearer picture on what a PC version of the game should look like.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Now That I've Played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, Here's What I Want Out of the PC Version
sources.text: This is an opinion piece by Jackie Thomas, IGN's Senior Tech Editor who's been covering PC games and the components that make them run for more than a decade. GTA 6 is exclusive to consoles at launch, but everyone knows a PC version will come out eventually. And when it does, it'll probably be the best way to play the game, provided you have the hardware to run it at a high frame rate. While I know that's a tough bar to clear with prices being what they are these days, after playing GTA 6 all day yesterday on everything from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro , I'm forming a clearer picture on what a PC version of the game should look like. Obviously, the first thing that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to be able to do that the console version can't is actually hit 60fps. Rockstar itself came out and said that a 60fps patch won't be coming to the PS5 Pro because it's simply not powerful enough. That wasn't super surprising . The PC version will be able to hit 60fps, but I think it might be a bit of a struggle for a lot of the PCs out there. Every single current-generation console is housing an AMD Zen 2 CPU with 8 cores and 16 threads. If we were going off core counts alone, that would match or exceed the vast majority of gaming PCs out there, according to the most recent Steam Hardware Survey . However, in the six years since Zen 2's debut in the Ryzen 7 2700X, IPC (Instructions per Clock) performance has risen so much that I doubt most recent 8-core CPUs are going to have the same troubles with players blowing shit up in GTA than the consoles have right now. The problem is, unlike graphics cards , CPUs are often one of the last things people upgrade in their PCs, so I imagine there are still a lot of older 8-core CPUs out there that aren't dramatically faster than what you'd find in the PS5 and Xbox Series X. But if you do have a more recent mid-to-high end CPU like the AMD Ryzen 7000 or 9000 series or anything Intel post 12th-gen, you should be able to push GTA 6 to a higher frame rate than the consoles. As I write this, I'm sitting next to a rig with an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 , and if the furthest I can push this game is 60fps, I don't even know if it's going to be worth double dipping. The real difference to GTA 6's frame rate on PC probably isn't going to come from the brute force of the hardware, but the software suites. Rockstar did some excellent work with the upscaling solutions available to them, and even used FSR 4.1 to great effect to get the game running as well as it did on the Xbox Series S. But, as good as FSR and PSSR are, they just aren't as good as DLSS. My hope would be that Rockstar makes full use of Nvidia's software suite to both make for cleaner upscaling and frame generation. I know that frame gen is a controversial technology, but a game like GTA 6 is perfect for it. After all, it's a slower paced single-player open world game that doesn't need you to have lightning-fast reflexes to succeed, so the added latency won't really be a big deal. I'll probably finish the game at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, and I'm already pretty used to that frame rate. On PC, I'll be fully expecting to use frame gen to push that number up to 240fps on my monitor, which will make the game much smoother and easier on the eyes. GTA 6's move to PC is going to be about more than just upping the frame rate though. As good as the game looks on console – and it looks f**king incredible – it's going to look even better on a PC that can push it to its limits. While the PS5 Pro uses ray traced global illumination, reflections and shadows, then pairs it with PSSR for a clean, beautiful image with excellent lighting, there are still some dials Rockstar can turn to bring the game to another level. Chief among these is going to be path tracing. Back when Cyberpunk 2077 implemented its 'RT Overdrive' preset, it completely changed the way the game looked. Using the PS5 Pro version of GTA 6 as a baseline, path tracing could elevate the game to a point where it's eerily close to photorealism. Of course, implementing path tracing would have a huge hit to performance, and GTA 6 isn't exactly going to be a walk in the park for most gaming PCs. For the most part, lighting settings would hammer your graphics card, and the biggest limiting factor for GTA 6 performance on console right now is the CPU, rather than the GPU. Again, it's hard to get metrics to see exactly how hard each processor in the PS5 Pro is being hit by GTA 6, but if the majority of the processing is being done on the CPU, adding more work for the GPU to do while it waits for the CPU probably isn't going to affect performance as much as you'd think. Word on the street is that the PC version of GTA 6 is going to come sooner than in past generations. I personally hope Rockstar uses the PC port as an opportunity to create the ultimate version of the game. Luckily, that's exactly what it did with Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5, even if they both had buggy launches. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. sources.title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
sources.text: The PS5 triggers are changing how I drive in GTA. Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me. But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6 . GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff. Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point. I've been calling this low-speed mode . At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode. Don't worry, it's not hard to fully gun it either: Just pull the trigger with a little gusto and you're off to the races. This is what the two speeds look like: This has completely changed how I drive in GTA. I'm already someone who takes these games slowly, but the natural stopping point of the throttle makes this easy and natural—as if Rockstar is not just allowing for a more immersive playstyle, but endorsing it. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. It's just a different experience than having to manually learn the speed thresholds and intuitively hold the trigger at an exact middle point. This is more like I'm pulling the trigger to one natural stop for "slow", and another for "fast". It's the four-wheeled equivalent of Jason and Lucia's walk (you have to press L3 to enter a jog or sprint), or the default saunter of Red Dead Redemption 2's horses. I can only recall one other open world game with a similar feature: the older Mafia games had speed limit toggles that automatically prevented cars from surpassing the speed limit. I always liked that, too, but this is more elegant. It turns out Rockstar's co-branding campaign that insists GTA 6 "plays best on PS5" isn't just marketing. In these months before GTA 6 is a PC game , I really would suggest you play it on a PlayStation for the controller perks alone. And when the time comes, I hope Rockstar goes the extra mile to port these DualSense features to the PC version. sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Players Are Surprised at How Well the Xbox Series S Handles GTA 6
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's launch, one of the biggest questions players were pondering was how well the Xbox Series S would handle Rockstar's highly anticipated game. Now that it's out in the wild, Series S owners are celebrating the fact that it actually runs the game pretty well on the console. All of the marketing footage leading up to GTA 6's launch was running on either the PS5 or the PS5 Pro, both of which are much more powerful than the Xbox Series S. When gameplay was finally revealed in August running at 30fps on the PS5, people understandably got a bit nervous about the Xbox Series S. But, thanks to Microsoft and AMD porting FSR 4.1 to the Xbox Series S last month, the game runs surprisingly well. It's not hard to see why so many people love the Xbox Series S. It's far and away the most cost-effective method to get a current-generation console, even after this year's price increases shot the price up to $499 . Even at that cost, it's still cheaper than the Nintendo Switch 2, and Nintendo's handheld can't play GTA 6. Sabía que tarde o temprano la gente iba a ver el valor de la xbox series S https://t.co/bHdgBCqweK Unsurprisingly, now that the Series S can decently handle GTA 6 (albeit with some frame drops here and there), Series S owners have been celebrating. Over on X/Twitter, user Scavenger928 posted a photoshopped image of Michael Jordan hugging the Series S, with a caption that translates to, "I knew sooner or later people would see the value of the Xbox Series S." Over on Reddit, there are several posts in the Xbox Series S subs from players who are surprised at how well the game holds up on the little Xbox. User either-ambition-9846 posted their findings about the port, surprised at how well GTA 6 runs, capping it off by saying, "I think the main point I want people to take away if you’re concerned about how well it’s going to perform, you’ll get immersed into the storyline and gameplay, the little frame drops that you might notice at the start, will slowly fade away. It’s a beautiful game, just go and enjoy it and forget about the squabbling on here." In the comments to that post, one user, shoddyartichoke2365 was even surprised that running GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S didn't cause the poor thing to melt, saying, "It's not too noisy or hot, surprisingly just as warm as it is on other games." GTA 6 has been received extremely well across the board. It's already tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the best-reviewed game of all time. Here at IGN, we gave it a 10 out of 10, where reviewer Luke Reilly called it, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played." When I tested GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S in the wee hours of the morning yesterday, I was also surprised at how well the 1440p machine handled the game. I can still absolutey tell the difference between it and the Xbox Series X version, but the game plays well, despite dropping frames occasionally. And, if anything, the game running as well as it does on the Xbox Series S bodes well for the inevitable PC version – maybe playing it on a handheld gaming PC won't be totally out of the question. sources.text: With there being cats, dogs, and 'gators all over Leonida, you should know how to pet animals in GTA 6 Knowing whether you can pet animals in GTA 6 should be one of the first questions you ask yourself, as it should in any game with animals in, to be honest. And, as ever, there's loads of wildlife in GTA 6 - though despite how it might sound above, I don't suggest you try and pet the alligators. Dogs and cats, though, can absolutely be played with and, provided you're making an effort to win Lucia back, you may come across one of the cutest cats we've ever seen pretty early on in Chapter 1, though it's not obvious how to interact with them. So, don't get too distracted, but here's how to pet animals in GTA 6. To pet animals in GTA 6, you need to approach them and press L2 or LT, which gives you the option to praise them. Praise them a few times and you'll finally see the option to pet them, though this doesn't always work. This is effectively the same as interacting with NPCs, but the option doesn't appear in the bottom of the screen for animals, meaning it's not so clear how to do so. By pressing L2 or LT on an unidentified animal also gives you the option to 'Study' them, which is the only way to add them to your collection of all the GTA 6 animals . You might also see the option to 'Scold' them, but we don't do that. Ever. Of course you won't be able to pet all animals, just the domesticated ones, but there are different breeds to find, so do make sure you interact with, study, and of course pet every dog and cat you see. The one seen in the images above are of the adorable grocery store employee that you'll find in Key Lento Mini Mart, so go stock up on supplies and meet them while you're at it. In fact, if you're working on improving your GTA 6 relationship status with Lucia, you should pick up some groceries before picking her up from jail. sources.title: How to make money in GTA 6
sources.text: What is the best way to make money in GTA 6? GTA 6 is finally here and players around the world are getting a chance to jump in to the world of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 years. However in GTA 6, money isn’t easy to get early in the game, and as such players have been looking for a way to make money fast in GTA 6. In this guide we’ll list the best ways to make money and GTA 6 from early game stick-ups which you can do almost from the start of the game, to later-game bank robberies which will yield the highest rewards but are also the most difficult. If you are enjoying GTA 6 you should check out our GTA 6 Guides Hub and make sure you bookmark it. We will be updating that hub every day for the forseble future with new guides new walkthroughs and everything you need to know about Grand Theft Auto 6. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Robbing groceries stores in Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the fastest ways to make money though you might not make a lot of it. Every groceries store in the game can be robbed. You can do this by going up to the cashier and sticking them up with a weapon. To do this approach, the cashier and hold the L2 button. This will aim your gun at the cashier without firing however at this point you can now interact with the cashier and threaten them which will cause them to open the cash register. You won’t get a lot of cash doing it this way, however there is little police response when you rob groceries stores. Some grocery stores also have a safe in the back room or you can access by kicking down the door or forcing the employee to open it for you. If that safe has a code you can often find the code on a post-it note located near the safe, or you can threaten the employee and you will get an option to ask them about the safe code. Eventually the police will be contacted and they will turn up at the store but by that point you should be long gone. It’s also worth noting that a lot of grocery stores have secret rooms of that sometimes include gang activity. you can tell if one of the grocery stores has a secret room by checking the minimap if there is a room that you haven’t accessed yet try picking the lock off the door or going back outside and checking another entrance. When you first get the ability to sell drugs, you can start robbing gang hideouts which often contain large amounts ofÂ various drugs that sell for a lot of money. This is by far one of the best ways to make money in GTA 6. The type of drug that the gang hideout is hiding has a huge effect on what it is worth for example things like weed are fairly cheap, but things like crystal and cocaine are far more expensive. You will know you are near a gang hideout because when will drive past and a yellow icon will appear on your map. At this point it is worth checking out what is there and if you check on the map you can also see the valuables that are available and that gang hideout If you steal drugs from a gang hideout you will have to physically take them to somewhere that you can sell them. However, later in the game if you do a lot of drug selling, some buyers will allow you to drop the drugs and a garage. Keep in mind, however, they will arrange a pick up and this means they will take a bigger cut of the money. Robbing jewellery stores and pawn shops is also a great way to make money in GTA 6. Howeverm these jewelry stores and pawn shops often have a high level of security so you are going to want to do some reconnaissance before you attempt to rob them. A lot of jewelry shops can be accessed from the back of the shop, where you will also be able to disable their security systems or if they have CCTV camera footage,Â you can destroy it.Â Doing this will delay the response time of the police, which is important because stealing from jewelry shops or pawn shops gets you a higher wanted level than stealing from a grocery store. One of the best ways to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is by completing main story missions. Often these main story missions will give you a big chunk of cash, so it’s worth doing as many of them as you can. This also applies to side missions which often provide you with a lot of cash. Just remember to take it to the bank to put in your account or it could be a lost if you are arrested or die. If you don’t have a bank account yet, check out our guide to Buck Me.Â Another great way to make money in GTA 6 is to sell cars. You will gain the ability to sell cars to Moses when you reach chapter 2 of GTA 6. He will take cars that do not have a tracker on them. On average you will get between $1000 and $5,000 dollars per car that you sell to Moses. After you sell a car to Moses there is a cooldown period where you can no longer sell cars to him however if you sleep at the safe house this cooldown period will elapse. Later in the game you can sell higher value cars to another prominent side character that is introduced and a later chapter . The ultimate way to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is to rob a banks.Â You won’t be able to rob banks straight away, in fact you will have to wait until you get the dye pack jammer during a mission where you rob a bank with a prominent side character. After this, you can rob banks whenever you like and it is by far the easiest way to make a huge amount of money in the game. Bank robberies are split up into several sections. There are basic cash drawers which you can get by threatening the tellers, there are safe which hide large numbers of marked bills, and then there are the bank vaults which house the largest amounts of money and in the game. With that being said, because of the amount of money you can get from robbing a bank, actually robbing a bank is also one of the most difficult things to do in the game. The police response is huge as soon as they are called so make sure you’re escape plan

sources.title: Former GTA 4 and Red Dead boss thinks "we are one Toy Story moment away" from people accepting gen-AI in game development in the West
sources.text: "In the East, they've already accepted it." Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'. "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business . "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it." Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it." Feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes. "A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay." Feder views gen-AI simply as new technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server. "That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder said of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected." There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding . More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it . Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development . Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs . Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront , the 'enshittification' of fan wikis , or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

sources.title: Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect
sources.text: Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2." I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff. There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse. That is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's important to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box. Gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions. And unlike in Red Dead's lawless towns, the NPCs of Leonida seem to react negatively to the guy walking around with assault rifles on his back. The game tells you early on that police pay closer attention to you when openly carrying firearms—another reason to stow them away when you don't need 'em. The car trunk is also where extra outfits can be stored. You can bring along five by default (more than Red Dead's saddles allowed), and even this isn't just for vanity. GTA 6's wanted system goes further than police chases: if you lose the cops, your wanted level will linger and cops identify you based on your description, clothes, and your car. The easiest way to go incognito after raising cain is to pull over, pop the trunk, and change outfits. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. It's all very smart and cool and I love it. Though I can also understand why others wouldn't—it's a significant break from what GTA has been up to this point. The two gun limit means murderous rampages might end earlier than they used to, and I can foresee getting annoyed the first time I bring a sniper rifle to a shotgun fight and have no way to correct that. But I think this reflects how Rockstar designed GTA 6 to be just as much a life sim as a crime fantasy. GTA 6 wants me to constantly make choices and consider what a real human would do. Like in one mission last night, I was left alone without my personal vehicle for the first time. Instead of Rockstar suggesting I grand theft an auto, a tutorial popped for calling a cab. So yea, I took a yellow cab back to my car a few miles away, and it was a chill ride, except for the cabbie who rudely shot down my attempts to make small talk. He's lucky my guns were in my car. sources.title: GTA 6 VP: "25 years on, the DNA remains" from Rockstar's original Vice City to modern Leonida
sources.text: Vice City has changed a lot over the years - but maybe less than you think With GTA 6 now so tantalizingly close that it's in the hands of players willing and able to pull off the New Zealand trick , it's very easy to get caught up in the now. After a 13-year wait for GTA 6, it can be easy to forget that all of the other GTA games were made over the span of just 12 years . But that's not what happened at Rockstar, as Stuart Petri, VP of art for 2D/UI design lays out - instead, he says that GTA 6 was the result of an uninterrrupted, 25-year process. In Rockstar's development notes, shared with press ahead of the GTA 6 review drop, Petri notes that "almost 25 years ago, we helped bring Vice City to life." That first foray to Rockstar's take on Florida "began as a simple visual design language," but has since "evolved into something far more sophisticated, layered, and considered." As Rockstar returns to Vice City for the first time since 2006's Vice City Stories, Petri notes that "we're returning to a world that has grown enormously in detail, creativity, and gameplay complexity." That meant that the series' art had to change too, ensuring it was relevant to a modern audience while "retaining the heritage that makes it unmistakably GTA." Petri discusses plenty about the discipline of UI art, but it's the underlying message about the history of Grand Theft Auto and the wider GTA identity that I think is most interesting. This series feels like such a known quantity, but it's really not - the world has changed an awful lot since 2013, and that's before we even touch on the differences in the gaming industry. Rockstar is releasing this game into a landscape that's wildly different to the one they last launched a Grand Theft Auto game into, but that doesn't seem to have phased Petri at all. In his part of the game, he says, "it's about building on that heritage" that the series thrives on, "and creating something that feels both entirely new and, at the same time, unmistakably GTA." He finishes by saying that "25 years on, the DNA remains," tying the very first version of Vice City to the one that we're all about to experience.
